overview: The V-wing is a starfighter whose service history spans Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). A fast arrowhead interceptor that escorted Palpatine's shuttle and became an early Imperial mainstay. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~7,200 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the V-wing during the political tensions that defined Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a starfighter, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the V-wing entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. A fast arrowhead interceptor that escorted Palpatine's shuttle and became an early Imperial mainstay. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~7,200 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the starfighter could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the V-wing symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The V-wing illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its starfighter layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~7,200 units hulls served during Clone Wars (22–19 BBY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the V-wing remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
